items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: This was taken on a tour with Randy Weston... This is Randy of course, this is Talib Kibwe, this is Stafford James and me

ctx.x: He seems like a very spiritual person, reading his liner notes and so forth.

Oh he is. Exceptionally spiritual. He is the most scholarly person I know. And he’s done his research in libraries in Morocco, Germany — these guys man, it’s amazing to be with them. Randy, Talib Kibwe, Neil Clark and this time I think there was a bass player from France who played with us, James — well I’m going to shoot myself — but I think he has a name like Williams or something. At any rate, these guys are always on, when we have a day off, they’re out somewhere doing research in the library or something.

It reminds me of something I remember you saying, and I’m going to quote you now, from our first interview. You said, “Most successful musicians understand humankind. Whether you’re talking to a president or a porter you should be able to communicate.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: he’ll perform with just himself, an alto player Talib Kibwe, and an African percussionist... I’m like the fifth member I think that’s added to the band.

ctx.x: I want to ask you something. Now for some people that type of guidance is too loose. For other people that’s exactly what they want.

Well he knows what he’s got. He knows he couldn’t say that to anybody you know. So I feel like I am chosen by him and, to make matters better, he pays very well. If he can’t — he performs in all configurations, from solo to symphony. So sometimes, a lot of times he’ll perform with just himself, an alto player Talib Kibwe, and an African percussionist. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

And he performs all over the world, Venezuela, and, but, if the budget can afford to pay me decently, then I’m added. I’m like the fifth member I think that’s added to the band. But if he can’t pay what he’d like to pay, he just won’t hire you. This is good. I like it. So I know whenever he calls it’s a well paying gig and no nonsense.
